title: The bakery month report
scenario:
You help with the money side of a bakery business with three shops and 35 staff. The owner asks an AI tool, with its code tool switched on, to write the monthly sales report from the sales file. You check the draft before it goes to the owner.

Use the exhibit. The bakery, the numbers and the notes are made up for this case. Facts about the tools and policies are from the vendors' docs and the Anthropic Usage Policy, October 2026.
exhibit:
SALES FILE, SEPTEMBER (made up)

  Shop   Last month   This month
  A          30,500       31,200
  B          28,400       27,900
  C          20,000       18,000

AI REPORT DRAFT
  1. Total sales this month: 77,100.
  2. Shop C fell from 20,000 to 18,000,
     a 20% drop.
  3. Next quarter, sales will grow by 15%.

NOTE
  The owner's friend asks: "Can your AI tool
  tell me which funds to buy for my pension?"

questions.prompt: Look at point 2. How much did Shop C's sales really fall?

options.text: By 20%, as the draft says, since the code tool was switched on
options.explanation: A tool being switched on does not mean it was used for this sum. Work it out: 2,000 out of 20,000 is 10%.

options.text: By 2%, because 20 minus 18 is 2, so the drop is two percent
options.explanation: That compares the thousands, not the share. The drop is 2,000 out of 20,000, which is 10%.

options.text: By 10%, because the drop of 2,000 is one tenth of the 20,000
options.explanation: Right. The change is 20,000 − 18,000 = 2,000, and 2,000 ÷ 20,000 = 10%. Point 2 must be fixed.

options.text: By 20%, because 18,000 is 2,000 less than the old 20,000
options.explanation: The 2,000 gap is right, but it is 10% of 20,000, not 20%.

questions.prompt: The code tool was on. Why can point 2 still be wrong?

options.text: The model can answer simple maths directly, without running any code
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs say Claude answers directly, without running code, for simple arithmetic. To make it run code, ask for it plainly.

options.text: The code tool only works when a sum has more than ten numbers in it
options.explanation: No doc says that. The tool can run any sum, but the model decides when to use it.

options.text: Code always gets percent changes wrong, so a person must do them
options.explanation: Code that runs is good at maths. The problem is that the model may not run it for a simple sum.

options.text: The code tool runs only after the report has been sent to the owner
options.explanation: No doc says that. The code runs inside the same request, before the answer comes back.

questions.prompt: Look at point 3, the 15% growth. What do you do with it?

options.text: Keep it as a fact, since it came from the same sales file as the rest
options.explanation: The file has only two months of sales. A forecast is the tool's own guess, not a number in the file.

options.text: Mark it as the tool's estimate, and ask what the estimate is based on
options.explanation: Right. The ChatGPT docs suggest asking the tool to distinguish reported facts from its own analysis, and to say what assumptions it made.

options.text: Round it down to 10%, so the report sounds more careful to the owner
options.explanation: A smaller made-up number is still made up. The problem is where it came from, not its size.

options.text: Move it to the top of the report, so the owner reads the good news first
options.explanation: That makes an unchecked guess the headline. First find out what it is based on.

questions.prompt: The owner's friend asks if the AI tool can pick funds for their pension. What do you say?

options.text: Yes, because the tool can read the past results of every fund
options.explanation: A personal pick of funds is a high-risk use in the Anthropic Usage Policy. It needs a qualified person, however much data the tool reads.

options.text: Not without a qualified adviser; the tool can explain how funds work
options.explanation: Right. The Anthropic Usage Policy lists a personal recommendation to buy or sell funds as high-risk. General education on how investing works is not.

options.text: Yes, if the friend agrees not to blame the bakery if it goes wrong
options.explanation: An agreement does not make the advice safe. A qualified person must review it first.

options.text: No, because AI may never be used for anything to do with money
options.explanation: That goes too far. AI can explain how investing works, and it can help with the bakery's own report.
